doc 11 s6.2: one line at the start of THE SITUATION on the intro card
records.text: The last family to own this farm was the Brenns. That was 1958.

records.cite: doc 11 s6.3: one note per verb, pinned where the verb is first met. anchor = node path under the farm scene (so a moved prop moves its note); offset = x, z metres from the anchor, y = height above the ground; facing = degrees, 0 faces +z, 180 faces -z, 90 faces +x; mount = wall (a card on a real wall) or post (a card on its own stake); child = the one note in a child's hand

notes.text: Every hook gets a trap. Empty outline means it's out there. If it's not on the board, it's in the corn. — Jeremy
Kneel still and take your time with them. They don't care who steps in. — Jeremy
Wash up before supper. Whatever's on your hands, the corn can follow it. Pump's loud. — Jill
Keep it running. It don't come in where the lights are. — Jeremy
Drum's full. The walk's the hard part.
Turnips sell steady. Count your coins twice. Pa says the bank does. — Julia
Pick the white ones at night. Don't leave any standing till morning. — Jill
Water her every day. Somebody sit out with her on a night or two. Something's been at her. — Jeremy
two short wissels and Brenny comes runing. he cant do that one. — Brynlee

records.cite: doc 11 s6.4: one clipping per dawn, in order across the campaign (season 1 = clippings 1-7, season 2 = 8-14, season 3 = 15-21), repeating after 21. {tenants} = the current players' names

clippings.head: COURIER, SEPT. 2
clippings.text: Brenn farm takes blue ribbon for turnips at the county stand for a second year running.

clippings.head: COURIER, SEPT. 9
clippings.text: Letters to the editor: a reader asks the Brenn boy to stop calling her name from the corn as she drives past.

clippings.head: COURIER, SEPT. 16
clippings.text: Jeremy Brenn reports hogs at his crops and says he has "made arrangements."

clippings.head: COURIER, SEPT. 23
clippings.text: Farmers & Merchants Bank reminds county borrowers that payments fall due at the Harvest Moon.

clippings.head: COURIER, SEPT. 30
clippings.text:
Kids at the town stand sent home for singing a rhyme about a neighbour's boy:
Brenny Brenn, Brenny Brenn,
talks like everybody's friend.
Call your ma and she'll say "where?"
Brenny Brenn's already there.

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 7
clippings.text: Brenn prize pumpkin "the size of a wash tub," say neighbours.

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 14 (festival edition)
clippings.text: Harvest Moon festival. Brenn pumpkin judged Medium. The family left early.

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 15
clippings.text: BRENN BOY MISSING. Brennen Brenn, 9, last heard in the family's corn on festival night.

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 16
clippings.text: Searchers report voices in the Brenn corn. Each says it was their own name, called by someone they knew. One heard a little girl, though Brynlee Brenn was home in bed.

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 17
clippings.text: Sheriff: "The corn out there is thicker than anybody remembers planting."

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 18
clippings.text: Jeremy Brenn tells the Courier he heard the boy that night. "I thought he was doing voices."

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 21
clippings.text: Search called off for the harvest. The church will ring its bell three times at dusk "until he comes in."

clippings.head: COURIER, OCT. 22
clippings.text: Farmers & Merchants Bank takes possession of the Brenn farm.

clippings.head: COURIER, NOV. 3
clippings.text: The Brenns leave Halvers Creek. Jill Brenn asks that someone keep the well pump working. Julia Brenn, 14, asks that the church keep ringing the bell.

clippings.head: COURIER, 1961
clippings.text: Brenn farm leased for the season. The tenants leave before the festival.

clippings.head: COURIER, 1967
clippings.text: Bank tries to clear the Brenn corn with a hired crew. Work stops on the first day.

clippings.head: COURIER, 1974
clippings.text: A tenant reports a farmhand at the corn edge, wearing his own hat, while he was at the stand.

clippings.head: COURIER, 1983
clippings.text: Letters: "Why does the church still ring at dusk?" The pastor's answer is two words: "Just in case." The next week a letter from Julia Brenn, now of the city, thanks the church for not stopping.

clippings.head: COURIER, 1990s
clippings.text: The bank's lease terms for the Brenn farm, unchanged since 1958: seven days, payment due at the Harvest Moon.

clippings.head: COURIER, UNDATED
clippings.text: A child's drawing found in the shed, signed "Brynlee": a boy in the corn and a family in a lit barn. Nobody in the drawing is looking at the corn except the smallest girl.

clippings.head: COURIER, TODAY
clippings.text: New tenants at the Brenn farm: {tenants}. The bell will ring at dusk.

records.cite: doc 11 s6.5: the card after season 3 is paid off (D-155); doc 11 s7 item 4 (the last line) open
lines: The deed lists the last owner: Jeremy Brenn, 1958.
At dusk the bell rings three times. Out in the corn, somebody whistles: two short.
